title: evalqualitycheck: bash-fence detection is loose and nested fences break it; the flaky lint resolves shadowed consts
summary: Found by comment-reduction batch 26 (2026-09-26) and reported without changing code. (1) scanBashCommands treats any fence whose opening line contains 'bash' as a bash fence, and its ``` toggle mishandles a triple-backtick line inside a four-backtick fence. An eval's commands can be missed or misread. (2) lintFuncFlaky resolves any identifier that matches a package const name, so a local variable that shadows the const is read as the const's value. (3) TestCheck_CommitPresenceRange_HALT reads r.Commands[0] in its error message after the length check has already failed. (4) go/acs/regression/cycle1270's comment cites flakylint_exec.go:88; the phrase is now at line 43.
fix: Parse fences by their info string (the exact language token) and track fence length as CommonMark does. Resolve consts through go/types, or by scope, not by name. Guard the test's index. Drop the line reference.
acceptance: A ```bashful fence is not a bash fence, and a nested ``` inside a 4-backtick fence does not close it (tests)
A local shadowing a package const is not resolved to the const (test)
